headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenBBTerminal can feed financial data into Perplexity’s vendor-hosted search/RAG flow, creating leakage and unverified-output cascade risks; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP and stdin/stdout, but its profile shows no browser or filesystem read/write, and Perplexity has no clipboard or host-execution bridge. The pair lacks a documented direct channel where Perplexity can inject instructions back into OpenBBTerminal, so only unusual manual bridging is plausible.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Perplexity text into OpenBBTerminal prompts or MCP inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between agents during analysis runs.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from retrieved text.
Require human review before any OpenBBTerminal action based on Perplexity output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported text.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate workspaces and no shared queue.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while Perplexity uploads documents and sends queries to vendor APIs. If OpenBBTerminal content is forwarded into Perplexity, sensitive financial or licensed material can leave the local environment through Perplexity’s hosted backend. The pathway exists in default use; mitigations are not enabled by default.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs financial or licensed data into Perplexity prompts or uploads, leakage occurs.
IF Perplexity is used with uploaded PDFs or images containing sensitive OpenBBTerminal outputs, those contents flow to vendor-hosted processing.
mitigations: Avoid sending OpenBBTerminal outputs into Perplexity unless redacted.
Strip account numbers, tickers tied to private strategies, and licensed excerpts before upload.
Use Perplexity only on public or synthetic samples.
requires-engineering: route sensitive analysis through a local-only model.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP checks before any upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, but neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, or shell execution. OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs; Perplexity is vendor-hosted with browser access only. Overlap exists mainly in read/query workflows, so direct write-write conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through an added MCP or API integration, conflicts can emerge.
IF the operator grants OpenBBTerminal write access to a shared directory, overlap increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents read-only against shared resources.
Do not connect both to the same mutable API token.
Run them in separate sessions for the same project.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared datastore.
requires-engineering: separate credentials per agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG system with live web citations, and OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs and MCP outputs. If Perplexity’s synthesized answer is treated as authoritative by OpenBBTerminal or the operator, errors can cascade into financial analysis decisions. The pair lacks a built-in verification handshake, so the default pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses Perplexity output as a factual input without independent verification, cascades occur.
IF Perplexity returns stale or hallucinated citations that are then operationalized, downstream error increases.
mitigations: Require source verification before acting on Perplexity answers.
Cross-check any market fact against a second source.
Mark Perplexity output as advisory only in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation.
requires-engineering: insert a human approval gate before trades or reports.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and uploads documents for analysis. If regulated or licensed financial material is sent to Perplexity, residency, retention, or contractual-use constraints may be violated. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated financial records or licensed data are uploaded to Perplexity, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator requires local-only handling for a dataset, Perplexity use violates that requirement.
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets out of Perplexity.
Use Perplexity only for public-market research.
Review retention and privacy settings before uploads.
requires-engineering: route sensitive workloads to a compliant local environment.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement if required.
